root_cause.text: The vulnerability exists because `rseq_exit_user_update()` initializes `struct rseq_ids.node_id` using `ids.cpu_id` within the same brace-enclosed initializer list, relying on indeterminate evaluation order that caused the compiler to access the uninitialized `ids.cpu_id` field before assignment.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the original code `struct rseq_ids ids = { .cpu_id = task_cpu(t), ..., .node_id = cpu_to_node(ids.cpu_id), };` and the CVE description states Clang evaluated `cpu_to_node(ids.cpu_id)` before `ids.cpu_id` was initialized with `task_cpu(t)`, triggering a KMSAN kernel-infoleak.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement initializes struct rseq_ids with node_id set to ids.cpu_id within the same brace-enclosed initializer list before cpu_id is assigned. Due to indeterminate evaluation order in C, the compiler may access the uninitialized ids.cpu_id field when setting node_id, causing undefined behavior. This matches the root cause description where rseq_exit_user_update() relies on indeterminate evaluation order between these two fields.
